title: Values Outside a Written Interval
statement: Let $\mu,f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and $d,j,a\in\mathbb{N}$. If $a<d$ or $d+j\le a$, then after writing the first $j$ values of $f$ into $\mu$ starting at $d$, the value at $a$ remains $\mu(a)$.
hypotheses_covered: a is outside the interval: a < d or d + j ≤ a
replaced:
Let $\mu,f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and $d,j,a\in\mathbb{N}$. Define a function by
replacing $\mu(x)$ with $f(x-d)$ when $d\le x<d+j$, and leaving it equal to $\mu(x)$
otherwise. If $a<d$ or $d+j\le a$, then its value at $a$ is $\mu(a)$.
